items.headline: Tech Sell-off Drags Major Indices Down on Friday; Markets Closed Today
items.summary: U.S. equity markets concluded Friday's trading session, October 30, 2026, with significant declines across all major indices, driven primarily by a broad tech sector sell-off. Disappointing earnings reports from AI-focused companies and growing concerns over the return on investment for artificial intelligence infrastructure spending fueled investor pessimism. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite experienced their worst day since June. Today, October 31, 2026, markets are closed for the weekend.

items.headline: Intel Plunges on Weak Outlook
items.summary: Intel Corp. ($INTC) shares sank almost 29% to $65.27, marking its worst day since 1974, after the chipmaker's fourth-quarter revenue forecast fell significantly below analysts' expectations despite reporting stronger-than-expected Q3 profit.

items.headline: Solowin Holdings Drops Post-Split
items.summary: Solowin Holdings ($AXG) lost 44.73% to $2.05, with the significant decline tied to a recent 1-for-200 reverse stock split.

items.headline: Regeneron Surges on Strong Earnings
items.summary: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals ($REGN) surged 13.2% to $926.96 after reporting third-quarter earnings per share and revenue that comfortably beat analyst estimates.

items.headline: Grid Dynamics Posts Strong Gains
items.summary: Grid Dynamics Holdings ($GDYN) rose 40.8% to $13.36, making it one of the day's top performers, though no specific company announcement was immediately identified as the catalyst.

items.headline: Energy and Healthcare Lead, Tech and Communication Services Lag
items.summary: On Friday, the Energy sector (+1.91%) and Health Care sector (+0.45%) were among the top performers, alongside Consumer Staples (+1.41%) and Real Estate (+0.26%). In stark contrast, the Information Technology sector (-4.89%) and Communication Services sector (-1.29%) were the biggest laggards, reflecting the broader market's shift away from high-growth tech stocks.

items.headline: Q3 GDP Grows 3.4% Amid Inflation Concerns, Fed Holds Rates Steady
items.summary: The U.S. economy's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) expanded at an annual rate of 3.4% in the third quarter, an acceleration from the prior quarter, largely driven by robust consumer spending and significant investments by AI companies. Despite this growth, headline PCE inflation rose to 3.6%, fueling investor concerns. The Federal Reserve maintained its benchmark interest rate, though a December hike is largely anticipated with odds around 75-85%.

items.headline: Big Tech Earnings Highlight AI Spending Scrutiny
items.summary: Major tech companies reported Q3 earnings with mixed results. Alphabet ($GOOGL) saw its stock drop significantly on Thursday after missing earnings and revenue estimates, alongside negative free cash flow due to massive AI investments. Amazon ($AMZN) also fell after reporting weaker-than-expected profits and increased capital expenditures for AI. These reports intensified worries about whether heavy AI spending will yield quick enough returns for investors.

items.headline: Treasury Yields Decline as Investors Seek Safety
items.summary: The 10-year Treasury yield fell to 4.93% on Friday, down from 4.98% the previous day, as investors moved into U.S. government bonds, signaling a flight to safer assets amid market volatility. This occurred even as oil prices saw an increase.
